Subject: Compute profile & deployment reconciliation for Retailly POC

Alex — thanks again for taking the call earlier. Quick recap from our side and a proposed next-steps list so we keep momentum on the POC.

High-level notes from the demo:
- Retailly wants sub-200ms median generation for short lookups (search re-rank) and <1s for longer multi-turn summarization.
- Expected peak TPS: 140 requests/sec during promotional spikes; baseline TPS ~25 r/s.
- Typical prompt mix: 70% short (<=256 tokens), 25% mid (256-1024), 5% long (>1024) — we captured a sample token export (attached).

Open questions we promised to confirm:
1) Deployment preference: you said you're evaluating Hosted API for speed vs Dedicated for predictable cost & isolation vs Private VPC for regulatory needs — can you confirm which constraints (security, latency, budget) are highest priority?
2) Concurrency model: do you want strict per-request latency SLOs (favor more reserved concurrency) or are you flexible with best-effort batching to lower unit cost?
3) GPU preference: any procurement constraints (we know some teams prefer H100; others need L40S due to availability)?

Next steps (proposed):
- Retailly: confirm priority order (security | latency | cost) and any hard constraints by 2026-08-06.
- Redwood: we will return a short compute profile with two recommended Dedicated configurations (balanced latency-focused and cost-focused), plus a Hosted fallback plan if Dedicated capacity is delayed.
- Internal: Ben + Monica will draft GPU/throughput sizing and a capacity workbook. I attached the token profile CSV you shared and will follow with the workbook by EOD tomorrow.

Attachments: [attachment: retailly_token_profile.csv (CSV, 23KB)]

Thanks — Laura

Laura — thanks for the thorough recap. A couple clarifications from our side:

Priorities: security > latency > cost. We need customer data sanitized before it leaves our VPC for the POC (PII redaction happens upstream, but auditability is required). That pushes us toward Dedicated in a VPC or Private (on-prem is not an option right now).

Latency nuance: the 200ms median target is for the search re-rank path only — those are short prompts and are most latency-sensitive. Summaries can tolerate up to 1s.

GPU availability: we do have an internal procurement preference for H100-class for the POC if possible; we can consider A100 if H100 lead times are long.

Concurrency: flexible to start — we prefer Redwood to recommend a conservative concurrency plan that can be relaxed after the initial week of traffic.

Attached a small CSV with a few more sample requests (added a couple of peak-hour rows).

— Alex

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 07 Aug 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: initial Dedicated configs for Retailly (draft numbers)

Looping in a quick draft so Laura can send to Alex — I'm keeping the math explicit so we can iterate.

Assumptions (from token profile + Alex clarifications):
- Peak TPS: 140 r/s (spikes) for short requests. Baseline 25 r/s.
- Token distribution: short = 70% (avg 120 tokens), mid = 25% (avg 512 tokens), long = 5% (avg 1600 tokens).
- Latency SLO short path: median <200ms; tail (95th) target <350ms.

Option A — Latency-focused (H100 preferred):
- Hardware: 4 x H100 (each node supports lower-batch latency paths, high single-stream perf).
- Effective concurrent slots: 48 (we allocate smaller concurrency per GPU to keep latency tight).
- Expected sustained short-path throughput: ~160 r/s with conservative batching; headroom for 2x burst using autoscale.
- Cost: higher than A100 mix, but best for strict latency.

Option B — Cost-balanced (A100 + batching):
- Hardware: 6 x A100 (larger batching to improve throughput/cost).
- Effective concurrent slots: 120 (higher batching, slightly higher median latency but still within ~250-300ms for short path).
- Peak throughput: ~240 r/s sustained with batching; better unit cost but more variability at tail.

Notes about KV/prefix cache and token mix:
- With 70% short repetitive lookups, prefix/KV caching should reduce token compute for many requests. We'll account for ~20-30% compute savings once we confirm cache hit rates during the POC.
- For long requests (>1024 tokens), both configs will route to a separate pool to avoid blocking short-path latency. That can live on fewer, larger-memory nodes.

Action items for our deliverable:
1) Laura: send these two options to Alex with clear tradeoffs + ask for preferred GPU availability window.
2) Laura/Monica: produce the redwood_capacity_workbook_RTL-1347.xlsx with per-hour cost estimates, autoscale knobs, and a recommended initial concurrency policy.
3) Alex / Retailly: confirm whether VPC peering is acceptable or they require Private on-prem demo.

I'll attach a short worksheet next.

— Ben

Subject: Re: Compute profile & deployment reconciliation for Retailly POC

Alex — sending the two Dedicated configurations Ben drafted plus the cost workbook (attached). Key highlights to make the decision easier:

- Recommendation: Start with Option A (4x H100) in a Dedicated VPC-backed deployment. Rationale: your security requirement + need for predictable latency. H100 gives us the best single-stream latency for the short re-rank path and simplifies meeting your median <200ms SLO.
- Fallback: if H100 procurement timing is an issue, we can provision Option B (6x A100) and tune concurrency and batch windows; we'll expect ~15-25% higher tail latency but lower unit cost.
- Caching: enable prefix/KV caching from day one — we estimate a 20% compute reduction for short path after warmup. We included a conservative and optimistic hit-rate column in the workbook.
- Rollout plan: week 1 conservatively overprovision (50% headroom) + detailed traffic monitoring. Week 2: tune concurrency based on observed latency and cache hit rate.

Please confirm by EOD Wed 2026-08-11 if Retailly can sign off on Dedicated VPC + H100 preference so we can request capacity and start network peering steps. Also confirm whether procurement needs an SOW or a pricing sheet for their internal approval.

Thanks again — I'll be on standby for any redlines from procurement.

Laura Bennett
